market_specific_notes: USCIS recognises all state and local health departments as civil surgeons for one narrow purpose: “they are authorized to complete the vaccination assessments for refugees seeking adjustment of status.” In the Phoenix metro that body is Maricopa County Public Health. It is not a general-purpose route to the full examination.

Everyone outside that category needs a designated civil surgeon, and there is exactly one authoritative way to confirm designation — the federal locator. A clinic advertising “USCIS exams” is making a claim; the locator is the record.

USCIS states that “Many health insurance plans do not cover all portions of this examination.” In a market where clinics quote a low headline exam fee, the uncovered portions are usually where the rest of the money is.
Take the checklist below in order. Designation is the one item with a single authoritative answer; everything after it is a comparison, and comparisons are worthless if the office is not designated.
local_vetting_points: Search uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by ZIP code. Maricopa County is large; a city-name search and a ZIP search are not the same query.
Match the name in the locator to the name the practice bills under.
Ask whether the tuberculosis test is done on site and what happens if it is positive.
Ask what the office does when vaccination records are missing.
Ask who signs the form and how soon after the visit.
typical_cost_ranges: USCIS publishes no exam price and says why: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.”
Its advice is to call several offices, noting the cost “can vary significantly”.
Compare like with like: examination, tuberculosis and syphilis testing, missing vaccines, form completion, follow-up visit. Ask for those five lines separately.
Form I-693 has no USCIS filing fee — $0. The published figure attached to the case is the I-485 fee: paper $1,440 or online $1,390 for an applicant over 14.
payment_options: USCIS instructs applicants to check acceptable forms of payment with the office in advance.
Bring your insurance card and ask whether the practice takes the plan for immigration medical examinations specifically.
wait_time_notes: The appointment is rarely the bottleneck. Laboratory turnaround and a second visit for vaccines usually are.
Ask what the office's typical gap is between the examination and a completed, signed form when nothing goes wrong.
availability_notes: Confirm whether a fast appointment includes the completed paperwork or only the examination.
If a filing deadline is near, give the date on the phone and ask the office to confirm it can meet it.
named_resources_or_providers: USCIS Find a Civil Surgeon locator (official) — uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon
Maricopa County Public Health — maricopa.gov/publichealth. USCIS recognises local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment.
USCIS Form I-693 page — uscis.gov/i-693, for the current form edition and filing instructions.
Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: In Phoenix the public health body that matters here is the county, not the city. Maricopa County Public Health is the local health department USCIS recognises, and the distinction is worth knowing before you start searching city-branded services that cannot complete this form.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Search the federal locator by ZIP, not by city name.
Confirm the practice is listed there under its billing name.
Ask for the price in five lines: examination, labs, vaccines, form completion, follow-up.
Gather the vaccination records USCIS names before the visit.
Say whether the I-485 is going by mail or online.
Confirm the form edition and signing date.

heading: Phoenix: the county is the health department, and the locator is the only designation check
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 in the edition USCIS currently accepts.

Government photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence. For an applicant aged 14 or younger, USCIS accepts identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name — a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

Your vaccination or immunisation record, covering what USCIS names: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card, and payment in an accepted form.
vaccination_handling_notes: Bring the records. Without them the office will either repeat doses or order blood tests to prove immunity, and both add cost and a second visit.
Arizona operates a statewide immunisation information system through which residents can request their own record; ask the clinic which record format it accepts before ordering.
For refugees adjusting status, the vaccination assessment may be completed at a state or local health department under the USCIS blanket designation.
bilingual_support: The official locator filters by Languages Spoken across a long list of named languages. That entry is what the practice told USCIS, not what a website says.
Ask whether the language support extends to the paperwork review itself, which is where misunderstandings turn into corrections.
appointment_booking_notes: Decide before the exam whether the I-485 is going by mail or online. By mail the envelope stays sealed; online, USCIS instructs you to open it and upload the form, keeping the original and envelope until the case is decided.
Confirm the form edition and the intended signing date — only the 01/20/25 edition is accepted for signatures dated 3 July 2025 or later.
Ask whether the booked slot covers the examination only or the full path to a signed form.
Ask when the sealed packet will be ready and what a correction costs if the form comes back wrong. An office that has no answer to the correction question has not been asked it often.
